security_audit.summary: The apparent PowerShell invocation, badge URLs, and most backtick findings are documentation syntax, not executable behavior. remediation.suggestion: Use static project evidence, or require explicit confirmation and isolation before running any repository command.

content.user_title: Create Accurate READMEs From Project Code
content.value_statement: Project documentation becomes stale when it relies on assumptions. This skill inspects repository evidence and creates a tailored README with installation, usage, API, and license sections.
actual_capabilities: Inspects Node, Python, Go, Rust, and Java manifests for metadata, dependencies, scripts, and entry points.
Builds sections for the title, badges, description, installation, usage, APIs, contributing, and license.
Uses source comments and documented help output to describe public APIs and command usage.
Writes or updates README.md in the project root or a user-specified path.
Marks important unknown details with TODO labels instead of inventing facts.
Selects language-specific sections and command patterns from bundled templates.
limitations: Help commands are not guaranteed safe because project initialization can run before the help flag is processed.
Output quality depends on accurate manifests, source comments, scripts, and license files.
Badge images require network access, and build status remains a placeholder without verified CI configuration.
Bundled templates focus on Node, Python, Go, Rust, and Java projects.

use_cases.title: Document a New Repository
use_cases.description: Create a first README from existing manifests, entry points, scripts, comments, and license data.

use_cases.title: Refresh Stale Project Instructions
use_cases.description: Compare an existing README with current repository evidence and replace outdated installation or usage details.

use_cases.title: Improve Contributor Onboarding
use_cases.description: Produce clear setup, usage, API, contribution, and license sections for public collaboration.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic README
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a README for this repository. Use only verified project files. Include installation, usage, contributing, and license sections. Mark missing facts as TODO.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create initial documentation for an existing project.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing README
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing README against the repository. Correct stale commands and dependencies, preserve accurate content, and list each unresolved detail as a TODO.
prompt_templates.scenario: Refresh project documentation after code or dependency changes.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Command-Line Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for this command-line project. Identify entry points and manifest scripts. Do not execute project code. Derive examples from static files only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Document a local CLI while avoiding untrusted command execution.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Release Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release-ready README. Document verified APIs from comments, map build and test commands, include accurate badges, and summarize the repository evidence used.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare comprehensive documentation for a public release.

output_examples.input: Generate a README for this Node package from its current files.
output: A title and description based on package metadata.
Installation and usage sections based on verified package scripts.
Dependency, contribution, and license details supported by repository evidence.

output_examples.input: Update this Python project README without running project code.
output: Python setup guidance based on the detected package files.
Entry-point and API summaries derived from source and docstrings.
TODO labels for details that the repository does not establish.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding documentation for this Go service.
output: Verified build, test, and run guidance from the Go module and project files.
Public API notes supported by Go comments.
Contribution and license sections with unresolved facts clearly marked.

best_practices: Review every proposed command before publishing the README.
Keep unknown facts as TODO items until repository evidence confirms them.
Use static files instead of executing project commands when the repository is untrusted.
anti_patterns: Do not invent dependencies, commands, APIs, environment variables, or deployment steps.
Do not copy every template section when the repository lacks supporting evidence.
Do not publish placeholder badges or license claims as verified facts.

faq.question: Which project types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides specific guidance for Node, Python, Go, Rust, and Java, plus evidence-based documentation for other repositories.

faq.question: Can it update an existing README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can preserve accurate content while correcting details that conflict with current repository files.

faq.question: Does it invent missing project details?
faq.answer: No. It uses TODO labels when manifests, source files, comments, or licenses do not provide enough evidence.

faq.question: Will it run project commands?
faq.answer: It may run a local help command when considered safe. Untrusted repositories should use static analysis only.

faq.question: Can it generate API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes, when JSDoc, docstrings, Go comments, Rust documentation comments, or JavaDoc describe public interfaces.

faq.question: Where does it write the result?
faq.answer: It writes README.md in the project root unless the user requests another path.
